test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 17 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The circumference of the base of a cylindrical vessel is 44 cm and its height is 25 cm. How many liters of water can it hold? (Take pi = (22)/(7))
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Radius (r) = Circumference ÷ 2π = 44 × (7/44) = 7 cm.

Volume in cm³ = π × r² × h = (22/7) × 7² × 25 = 3850 cm³.

Convert to liters (1 L = 1000 cm³): 3850 ÷ 1000 = 3.85 liters.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.85 liters.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Circumference of the base = 44 cm

Height of the cylinder (h) = 25 cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/432e6e5f53b85a03ce756789427e0a3a3b45546f419701f54805c05ed3d8f13c.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Circumference of base = 2πr

Volume of cylinder = πr²h

1 liter = 1000 cm³

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r = 44

⇒ (44/7) × r = 44

⇒ r = 44 × (7/44)

⇒ r = 7 cm

⇒ Volume of cylinder = (22/7) × (7)² × 25

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 49 × 25

⇒ Volume = 22 × 7 × 25

⇒ Volume = 154 × 25

⇒ Volume = 3850 cm³

⇒ Capacity in liters = 3850 ÷ 1000 = 3.85 liters

**∴ The correct answer is 3.85 liters.**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

TSA = 2πr(r + h), where r is the radius of the base and h is the height.

Curved Surface Area of Cylinder

CSA = 2πrh. This represents the outer wall surface area, excluding the top and bottom circular faces.

Metric Volume Conversion

1 m³ = 1000 liters. Conversely, 1 liter = 1000 cm³ or 1000 ml.
